chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjajaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Al-Hameel, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is Al-Hameel?' I said: 'A woman is taken captive from her land, and with her is a young child, so she says, 'He is my son.' And a man is taken captive, so he meets his brother, so he says, 'He is my brother,' and they recognize each other, and there is no proof for them regarding that except their own words.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'What do those before you say?' I said: 'They do not inherit them, because there was no proof for them regarding that; rather, the birth was in Polytheism.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! If she comes with her son or her daughter with her, and she does not cease to affirm it, and when he recognizes his brother, and that was in soundness of their intellects, and they do not cease affirming that, they inherit from one another.'

key_terms.الشِّرْكِ: Al-Shirk (Polytheism, here referring to the state of captives before Islam)
key_terms.صِحَّةٌ مِنْ عَقْلِهِمَا: Sihhatun min aqlihima (soundness of their intellects)

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance determined for captives who recognize each other as family without formal proof?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that mutual recognition and continuous affirmation (*tawatur*) between captives are sufficient legal proof for inheritance, overriding the need for formal witnesses. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that practical continuity and self-identification can validate kinship ties even when formal documentation is absent, ensuring family rights are preserved during displacement.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about Al-Hameyl (brought from another land), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And which thing is Al-Hameyl?’ So I said, ‘The woman is taken prisoner from her land, and with her is the young child. So she is saying, ‘He is my son’. And the man is taken prisoner so he meets his brother, so he is saying, ‘He is my brother’. And they are both recognised as such, and there is no proof for them both upon that except for their own words’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What are the ones before you saying’. I said, ‘They would not be inheriting each other because there does not happen to be any proof upon that. But rather, the birth was in the Polytheism’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! (Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is free from all defects) She comes with her son or her daughter with her, and she does not cease to accept it, and when he recognises his brother, and that was in good health from their two intellects, and they both do not cease accepting that, they would inherit each other’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and a number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who is al-Hamil (brought from other land). He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is al-Hamil ?  I then replied, ‘A woman is taken captive from her land. With her is a small child and she says that he is her son. A man is taken as a captive, who meets his brother and says that he is his brother. They recognize each other but they do not have any proof and testimony except their words. He (the Imam) then asked, ‘What do people with you say about it? 5 I replied, ‘They do not give them any share of inheritance; they have no proof about their birth and it is birth in paganism. 5

He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah is free of all defects, when she comes with her son or daughter, continues confirming their relationship and when he recognizes his brother, both of them are in good health and they continue confirming it; they must inherit from each other.
[Note: The next several passages of the Arabic text are words of al-Fadl and are not translated.]
